ops.title: VAPID public key rides GET /api/push/vapid-key, not the pair payload
ops.body:
Decision (P2 Web Push): the web app fetches the VAPID public key from `GET /api/push/vapid-key` on the daemon's auth-guarded mux, instead of extending `access.PairPayload`.

Why:
- The pair payload is a one-shot QR minted at pair time; a key baked into it goes stale if `vapid.json` is ever re-minted, while an endpoint always serves the current key.
- A client needs the key at subscribe time in the browser (it already holds the base URL + bearer token from pairing), and re-subscription after SW churn must work without re-pairing.
- Fits the existing surface: consumer REST rides the daemon `Mux()` (cc-interact `examples/echo` mountREST precedent); registration is already `POST /api/push/subscriptions` on the same mux.
- P3 (iOS/APNs) won't use VAPID, so widening the pair payload buys nothing cross-platform.

Related: subscriptions persist as `push.subscribe`/`push.unsubscribe` events under well-known subject id `push` (deduped by endpoint via event DedupKey), projected into `push_subscriptions`; gone endpoints (404/410) are pruned append-first.
